about: Trial 3 (2026-09-23): t2 without its pair wording (E2 turned answers into a lone question), E1 reworded, the heat paragraph covering both ends, and the founder's reading of "on power grip" as a driver-words fact (bite-hold fact 1). Nets and KB edits here are the FOUNDER'S CALL.

edits.find: What the driver states is fact; never re-suspect it.
edits.replace: What the driver states is fact; never re-suspect it — and a change they say didn't help counts against the thing it works through, not just that one setting.
edits.why: s-02: rear toe gain offered after "Rear toe hasn't helped" (his never); the first wording (t1) held 1 of 4.

edits.find: EFFECT: more drive off the corner — both rear tyres put the power down — with more rotation on throttle; less rotation off throttle; biggest in tight corners
edits.replace: EFFECT: more rotation on throttle — the rear gives up side grip to put the power down — and more drive off the corner; less rotation off throttle; biggest in tight corners
edits.why: g-01 both tries led with a thicker diff for "How do I improve on power grip" — his never.

edits.find: EFFECT: less drive off the corner and less rotation on throttle; more rotation off throttle; too thin and it will not put the power down; biggest in tight corners
edits.replace: EFFECT: less rotation on throttle — more rear side grip on power — and less drive off the corner; more rotation off throttle; too thin and it will not put the power down; biggest in tight corners
edits.why: the mirror of the thicker side.

edits.find: the front rolls in faster, so the initial steering comes sooner — the same amount, there for longer, so it can feel like more; too far and it is too reactive
edits.replace: the front rolls in faster, so the initial steering comes sooner and the car reacts quicker to every input — the same amount, there for longer, so it can feel like more; too far and it is edgy and hard to drive
edits.why: his a-01 and s-05 notes: thinner oil makes it more reactive.

edits.find: than sharing the load evenly would, all else equal.
edits.replace:
than sharing the load evenly would, all else equal.

**Heat.** A tyre heats from the work it does — the force it carries times how far it slides — so it heats more the more of each corner it spends loaded, and the harder it is loaded. Stiffer in roll — a stiffer bar or spring, a higher roll centre, less flex — loads the tyres sooner, so they work for more of every corner ([[bite-hold]]); made at one end only, that end also takes a larger share of the load transfer, so its outside tyre is loaded harder than before ([[corner-regime]]). Toe heats a tyre by scrubbing it ([[toe-and-scrub]]).
edits.why: s-01: toe was the only heat mechanism in the KB; t2 wording (one end only) made it ask which end 2 of 2.

edits.find: end the driver wants moved, never as the end that is wrong.
edits.replace: end the driver wants moved, never as the end that is wrong. "Grip" on power with no end named is the rear holding on as the throttle comes in: lacking it is oversteer on power, not wheelspin (founder, 2026-09-23).
edits.why: g-01: "How do I improve on power grip" read as wheelspin/drive in every try; his must: "lack of on power grip is normally oversteer".
